questions.question: Which statement best captures the primary motivation for post-training quantization (PTQ) in large language models (LLMs)?
questions.choice_A: Reduce memory footprint and inference latency without requiring costly retraining or access to original training data.
questions.choice_B: Improve model generalization by adding quantization noise during training.
questions.choice_C: Increase training throughput by using smaller batch sizes.
questions.choice_D: Enable on-the-fly architecture search during deployment.

questions.question: In the context of per-channel range calibration for weights, what is the main advantage over per-tensor calibration?
questions.choice_A: It completely eliminates quantization error regardless of bit-width.
questions.choice_B: It allows each output channel to use its own scale, better capturing channel-wise variance and reducing distortion.
questions.choice_C: It enables dynamic quantization at runtime without calibration.
questions.choice_D: It only applies to activations and not to weights.

questions.question: Which core idea differentiates GPTQ from naive rounding-based PTQ?
questions.choice_A: It applies stochastic rounding during training.
questions.choice_B: It introduces per-layer temperature scaling.
questions.choice_C: It greedily quantizes weights with an approximate second-order (Hessian-aware) error model to minimize output error.
questions.choice_D: It relies on per-token reinforcement learning signals.

questions.question: Activation calibration in PTQ typically involves which procedure?
questions.choice_A: Fitting a Gaussian prior to weights and sampling.
questions.choice_B: Collecting representative inputs to estimate activation ranges or distributions for setting scales and clipping.
questions.choice_C: Pruning low-magnitude activations to zero during training.
questions.choice_D: Replacing ReLU with GELU to smooth distributions.

questions.question: What is a central insight behind SmoothQuant for LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Use ternary weights to exactly preserve attention logits.
questions.choice_B: Shift activation magnitude into weights via layer-wise affine rescaling, making activations easier to quantize at low bit-widths.
questions.choice_C: Quantize only embeddings and leave all other layers in floating point.
questions.choice_D: Apply random permutations to reduce outliers in keys and values.

questions.question: Why do LLMs often benefit from per-channel quantization of linear layer weights?
questions.choice_A: LLMs have uniform activation distributions across channels.
questions.choice_B: Attention heads and MLP channels can exhibit very different scales; per-channel scales avoid one channel dominating the quantization range.
questions.choice_C: Per-channel quantization reduces the number of parameters.
questions.choice_D: Per-channel quantization enables mixed-precision training.

questions.question: Which statement about AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization) is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: It quantizes activations but leaves weights in floating point.
questions.choice_B: It preserves a small subset of salient (often outlier) weights in higher precision using activation sensitivity to guide selection, while quantizing the rest.
questions.choice_C: It requires full model fine-tuning with a quantization-aware loss.
questions.choice_D: It focuses exclusively on KV-cache quantization.

questions.question: In practice, what is a common limitation of PTQ when pushing to 2-bit or 1-bit representations for LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Hardware cannot execute bitwise operations efficiently.
questions.choice_B: Calibration sets become too large to process.
questions.choice_C: Quantization error overwhelms signal in sensitive layers, often causing severe perplexity degradation without retraining or distillation.
questions.choice_D: The optimizer state becomes incompatible with low-bit formats.

questions.question: Quantization-aware linear layers and kernel replacement strategies primarily aim to:
questions.choice_A: Reduce the number of attention heads at inference.
questions.choice_B: Swap default GEMM/matmul kernels with integer-friendly implementations and fused dequantize/compute steps to realize actual speedups.
questions.choice_C: Increase the model’s parameter count to improve accuracy.
questions.choice_D: Replace softmax with a low-precision alternative during training.

questions.question: Which calibration objective is commonly used to set activation ranges for PTQ in LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Maximize cosine similarity between inputs and outputs.
questions.choice_B: Minimize mean-squared error (MSE) between float and quantized activations, possibly with percentile clipping to reduce outlier impact.
questions.choice_C: Minimize Kullback–Leibler divergence between weight histograms.
questions.choice_D: Maximize entropy of activation distributions.

questions.question: What is a practical trade-off when choosing post-training quantization over quantization-aware training (QAT) for LLMs?
questions.choice_A: PTQ generally achieves higher accuracy but is much slower than QAT.
questions.choice_B: PTQ is simpler and cheaper to apply since it avoids retraining, but it may incur larger accuracy loss, especially at very low bit-widths.
questions.choice_C: PTQ requires more labeled data than QAT.
questions.choice_D: PTQ can only be applied to encoder-only models.

questions.question: How does GPTQ use second-order information in practice?
questions.choice_A: It computes exact Hessians for every layer.
questions.choice_B: It approximates the Hessian or uses blockwise curvature estimates to guide greedy weight quantization that minimally perturbs layer outputs.
questions.choice_C: It estimates Fisher information from supervised labels.
questions.choice_D: It uses Laplacian approximations from graph-structured priors.

questions.question: Why do outlier activations pose a particular challenge for PTQ in LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Outliers reduce inference parallelism on GPUs.
questions.choice_B: Outliers force scales to be large, coarsening quantization for the bulk of values and increasing error unless clipped or redistributed.
questions.choice_C: Outliers make backpropagation unstable during PTQ.
questions.choice_D: Outliers invalidate symmetric quantization schemes mathematically.

questions.question: Which deployment consideration most often determines the real-world speedup from INT8 PTQ on GPUs?
questions.choice_A: Model’s vocabulary size.
questions.choice_B: Availability of optimized integer GEMM kernels and tensor core support, plus layout/fusion that minimizes dequantization overhead.
questions.choice_C: Choice of tokenizer.
questions.choice_D: Number of training epochs used pre-quantization.

questions.question: What is a common strategy to maintain LLM quality when quantizing to 4 bits with PTQ?
questions.choice_A: Use per-tensor symmetric quantization for all layers.
questions.choice_B: Adopt groupwise or blockwise per-channel quantization and retain certain outlier channels or weights at higher precision.
questions.choice_C: Quantize the embedding matrix more aggressively than attention layers.
questions.choice_D: Disable rotary position embeddings during calibration.

questions.question: In SmoothQuant, what role does the affine rescaling play across paired layers (e.g., linear and following normalization)?
questions.choice_A: It balances scales so that activations become more uniform and quantization-friendly while compensating in weights to preserve the computation.
questions.choice_B: It changes the model’s expressivity by reparameterizing attention.
questions.choice_C: It eliminates the need for calibration data.
questions.choice_D: It forces asymmetric quantization on all tensors.

questions.question: What is a key difference between weights-only quantization and full-precision activations versus full INT8 quantization of both weights and activations in LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Weights-only quantization typically yields smaller accuracy drops but limited speedups; quantizing activations can unlock larger speed and memory gains if kernels are optimized.
questions.choice_B: Weights-only quantization always outperforms full INT8 in speed.
questions.choice_C: Full INT8 quantization never requires calibration.
questions.choice_D: Weights-only quantization is incompatible with attention mechanisms.

questions.question: Why is PTQ particularly challenging for 1–2 bit quantization without retraining?
questions.choice_A: Scale and zero-point cannot be represented at such low precision.
questions.choice_B: The representational set is extremely coarse, causing large function approximation errors that often require loss-aware adaptation or distillation to correct.
questions.choice_C: Hardware does not support bitwise operations below 4 bits.
questions.choice_D: Embedding layers are invariant to bit-width.

questions.question: Which component of Transformer-based LLMs is often most sensitive to aggressive quantization and therefore may require higher precision or special handling?
questions.choice_A: Layer normalization parameters and attention projection layers.
questions.choice_B: Final logits softmax temperature.
questions.choice_C: Tokenizers and byte-pair merges.
questions.choice_D: Dropout masks.

questions.question: When replacing linear layers with quantization-aware kernels, what practical issue can negate theoretical speedups?
questions.choice_A: Integer arithmetic is slower than floating point on all GPUs.
questions.choice_B: Frequent dequantize–requantize operations and poor tensor layouts introduce overhead that limits throughput.
questions.choice_C: INT8 accumulators overflow on every operation.
questions.choice_D: Batch size must be 1 for correctness.

questions.question: What is a reasonable guideline for constructing a calibration dataset for PTQ of LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Use millions of labeled examples matched to the pretraining corpus.
questions.choice_B: A modest set (e.g., a few thousand representative prompts) that approximates deployment distributions is often sufficient to estimate activation ranges.
questions.choice_C: Only random noise inputs are needed to avoid bias.
questions.choice_D: Calibration is unnecessary if using per-channel quantization.
